## Sophia modules (sophia.html) · 24 passages

- **ep**: On February 21, 2025, weeks into her tenure, Attorney General Pam Bondi told Fox News that Epstein's client list was sitting on her desk right now to review, and described the release as a directive from the President. She later clarified she had meant the Epstein material generally rather than a specific list. Six days later the DOJ and FBI released the First Phase of Declassified Epstein Files — binders handed to conservative influencers on camera at the White House, which were then found to contain almost nothing that was not already public.
- **ep**: Bondi appeared before the House Judiciary Committee for more than five hours over the Department's handling of the files. Survivors sat behind her in the room. She did not offer them an apology. She traded personal attacks with committee members, calling Rep. Jamie Raskin a washed-up loser lawyer and accusing Rep. Thomas Massie — the Republican co-author of the Transparency Act — of Trump derangement syndrome. This is the hearing you watched, and the account of it is not a characterisation by critics: the exchanges are on the record and were reported identically across outlets.
- **ep**: In March 2026 the House Oversight Committee subpoenaed Bondi over the Department's handling of the files, with five Republicans joining Democrats in the vote. In April 2026 Trump fired her. On May 29, 2026 she gave a closed-door transcribed interview to House Oversight, telling the panel that redaction errors were made, that she had been assured by the reviewing team that only non-responsive, privileged or duplicative material was withheld, and that to the best of her knowledge the Department produced everything required. She refused to discuss the President's involvement in the handling of the files. Todd Blanche, her deputy, became acting Attorney General.
- **ep**: FBI staff were reportedly instructed to flag mentions of Trump while reviewing the document trove, and the Wall Street Journal reported that Bondi told Trump in May 2025 that his name appeared in the files. Two months later came the memo announcing no further disclosure. This module reports these as named-outlet reporting rather than as established fact — DOJ has not confirmed the flagging instruction — and reports the sequence without asserting causation between the briefing and the memo, because no document establishes that link.
- **ep**: In November 2025, despite the July memo stating no further investigation was warranted, Trump ordered Bondi to investigate Epstein's ties to Bill Clinton and other prominent Democrats. She said the Department would pursue it with urgency and integrity and assigned it to the US Attorney in Manhattan. The sequence is documented: the Department found no basis to investigate uncharged third parties in July, and in November was directed to investigate a specific set of named third parties. Both cannot rest on the same evidentiary standard.
